questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.hint: It is a muscle in your chest that beats.
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular pump that pushes blood through blood vessels.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
options: Your lungs stop working while you run
Your muscles need more oxygen and food, so blood must be delivered faster
The heart is trying to cool you down

mistakes.3: Sweating cools you; the heart rate rises to supply oxygen

questions.hint: Think about what working muscles need.
questions.explanation: Working muscles use more oxygen and glucose. The heart beats faster to carry more blood (and oxygen) to them.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?

mistakes.1: Veins carry blood back to the heart

questions.explanation: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Where does most digestion and absorption of food into the blood happen?

mistakes.3: The large intestine mainly absorbs water

questions.hint: It is a long, coiled tube after the stomach.
questions.explanation: Digested food is absorbed into the blood through the wall of the small intestine.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the main job of the lungs?
options: To filter waste from blood to make urine
To take oxygen into the blood and remove carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: In the lungs, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out to be breathed out.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which food group mainly helps the body grow and repair itself?
questions.hint: Found in eggs, beans, fish and meat.
questions.explanation: Proteins are used for growth and repair.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Put these in the order food passes through them: stomach, mouth, small intestine, oesophagus. Type them separated by commas.
questions.explanation: Mouth → oesophagus (food pipe) → stomach → small intestine.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A student’s pulse was 72 beats per minute at rest and 130 after exercise. Five minutes later it was 80. What does this show?
options: Heart rate rises during exercise and returns towards the resting rate afterwards
Resting makes the heart beat faster
questions.explanation: The pulse rose with exercise, then fell back towards 72 during rest — this is recovery.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why do doctors advise eating foods that contain fibre?
options: Fibre helps food move through the intestines and prevents constipation
Fibre carries oxygen in the blood
questions.explanation: Fibre is not digested but keeps the gut working well, helping food move through.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which organ filters the blood to remove waste and make urine?
questions.hint: There are two, in your lower back.
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter waste from the blood, producing urine.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which part of the blood carries oxygen?
questions.hint: Their colour comes from a substance that holds oxygen.
questions.explanation: Red blood cells carry oxygen around the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why is smoking harmful to the lungs?
options: Smoke damages the lungs, making it harder for oxygen to pass into the blood
Smoke gives the lungs extra oxygen
Smoke makes the heart beat more slowly so it rests
questions.hint: Think about what the lungs need to do.
questions.explanation: Chemicals and tar in smoke damage lung tissue, so less oxygen gets into the blood.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Predict what happens to breathing rate during exercise, and why.
options: It stays the same because breathing is automatic
It stops until the exercise is over
It increases, to take in more oxygen and remove more carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Breathing gets faster and deeper so more oxygen reaches the blood and more carbon dioxide is removed.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil and anchor the plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A plant is kept in a dark cupboard for two weeks. Its leaves turn yellow. Why?
options: Plants only need water, so it was over-watered
Without light the plant cannot make its own food
The cupboard was too cold for any plant
questions.hint: What do plants need light for?
questions.explanation: Plants use light energy to make food in their leaves. Without light they cannot make food and become weak and yellow.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the main job of the leaves?
options: To make food for the plant using light
To hold the plant in the soil
questions.hint: They are usually green and flat.
questions.explanation: Leaves capture light to make food for the plant.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is pollination?
options: When a plant takes in water
When a seed starts to grow
The transfer of pollen from the male part to the female part of a flower
When seeds are carried away from the plant
questions.explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther (male) to the stigma (female).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A seed has hooks that stick to animal fur. How is it dispersed?
questions.explanation: Hooked seeds catch in fur and are carried to new places by animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why is it useful for seeds to be dispersed away from the parent plant?
options: So the seeds can be eaten more easily
So new plants do not compete with the parent for light, water and space
So the parent plant can rest
questions.hint: What would happen if all seeds grew underneath the parent?
questions.explanation: Seeds spread out so seedlings are not competing with each other and the parent for resources.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT needed for a seed to germinate?
questions.explanation: Seeds need water, warmth and air to germinate. Light is needed later for growth, once leaves appear.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Celery is placed in water with blue food colouring. After a day the leaves have blue streaks. What does this show?
options: Water is carried up the stem to the leaves
questions.hint: Follow the path of the colouring.
questions.explanation: The coloured water travelled up tubes in the stem to the leaves, showing how water is transported.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why do many flowers have brightly coloured petals and a sweet smell?
options: To make more light for the leaves
questions.explanation: Colour and scent attract insects, which carry pollen from flower to flower.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What does the stem do?
options: Supports the plant and carries water to the leaves
questions.explanation: The stem supports the plant and transports water and nutrients.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Dandelion seeds have a light, fluffy “parachute”. How are they dispersed?
questions.explanation: The parachute catches the wind and carries the seed away.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Two identical plants are given the same water and light, but one is kept at 5 °C and one at 22 °C. Predict which grows better.
options: Both grow the same because they have the same water and light
The plant at 22 °C, because warmth helps growth
The plant at 5 °C, because cold helps growth
questions.explanation: Most plants grow better in warm conditions, so the plant at 22 °C should grow better.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, which is the producer?

mistakes.0: The Sun provides energy but is not a living producer

questions.explanation: Grass is a plant; it makes its own food using light, so it is the producer.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, what would probably happen to the grass if most of the foxes died?
options: No change, because foxes do not eat grass
More grass, because foxes eat grass
Less grass, because more rabbits would survive to eat it
More grass, because rabbits would die out
questions.explanation: Fewer foxes → more rabbits survive → rabbits eat more grass → less grass.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What do the arrows in a food chain show?
options: Which animal eats the arrow’s starting organism

mistakes.1: Close, but the arrow points to the eater, showing energy flow

questions.hint: Arrows point from the food to the eater.
questions.explanation: Arrows show the flow of energy from the organism eaten to the organism that eats it.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: An animal that eats only plants is called a…
questions.explanation: Herbivores eat only plants.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Use the key. An animal has six legs and wings. Which group is it in?
questions.hint: Start at question 1 and follow the answers.
questions.explanation: Six legs → question 2 → wings → insect.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How is a polar bear adapted to its cold habitat?
options: Thin skin to feel the snow
Dark fur to stand out from the snow
Thick fur and a layer of fat keep it warm
questions.explanation: Thick fur and fat insulate the polar bear; white fur also gives camouflage.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why do cactus plants have spines instead of wide leaves?
options: Spines lose less water and protect the plant from animals
questions.explanation: Spines have a small surface area so the cactus loses less water; they also deter animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Farmers spray a chemical to kill insects on crops. Birds in the area become fewer. Which is the best explanation?
options: The chemical made the crops grow taller
The birds migrated because it was winter
The birds had fewer insects to eat, or ate poisoned insects
Birds do not like the smell of crops
questions.hint: Think about the food chain crop → insect → bird.
questions.explanation: Killing insects removes the birds’ food, and birds that eat poisoned insects may be harmed.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which action would best help protect a local habitat?
options: Planting native trees and reducing litter
Building a car park on the meadow
questions.hint: Which choice gives living things food and shelter?
questions.explanation: Native trees provide food and shelter; reducing litter protects animals.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In the food chain leaf → caterpillar → bird → hawk, which animal is the top predator?
questions.hint: Nothing eats it in this chain.
questions.explanation: The hawk is at the end of the chain; nothing in the chain eats it.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which is a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: A frog has a backbone; the others are invertebrates.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In the food chain seaweed → limpet → crab → seagull, which organism is a prey but not a predator?
questions.hint: It is eaten, but only eats plants.
questions.explanation: The limpet is eaten by the crab, but it eats seaweed (a plant), so it is not a predator.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Camels have wide, flat feet. How does this help them survive in the desert?
options: They spread the camel’s weight so it does not sink into sand
They keep it cool by releasing heat
questions.explanation: Wide feet spread the weight over a larger area, so the camel does not sink into soft sand.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which statement describes the particles in a solid?
options: Close together but able to move past each other
Close together in a fixed pattern, vibrating in place
Not moving at all and spread far apart
Far apart and moving quickly in all directions
questions.explanation: Solid particles are tightly packed in a regular pattern and can only vibrate.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A puddle disappears on a sunny day. What has happened to the water?
options: It has evaporated and become water vapour in the air
It has melted into the ground

mistakes.0: Condensation is gas turning to liquid — the opposite

questions.hint: Heat turns liquid into a gas.
questions.explanation: The Sun’s heat makes liquid water evaporate into water vapour, a gas.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the change from a liquid to a solid called?
questions.explanation: Freezing is when a liquid turns into a solid.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which property makes copper a good choice for electrical wires?
questions.explanation: Copper is a good electrical conductor.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Water droplets form on the outside of a cold glass of juice. Where does the water come from?
options: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold glass

mistakes.3: Glass is not permeable; the water comes from the air

questions.explanation: Water vapour in the air cools when it touches the cold glass and condenses into liquid droplets.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does a gas fill any container it is put in?
options: Its particles are far apart and move freely in all directions
Its particles are heavier than air
questions.hint: Think about particle spacing and movement.
questions.explanation: Gas particles move quickly and freely, spreading out to fill the whole space.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which material would be best for a saucepan handle?
options: Steel, because it conducts heat well
Wood or plastic, because they are thermal insulators
questions.hint: You do not want the handle to get hot.
questions.explanation: Handles should be thermal insulators so heat does not travel to your hand.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Wet clothes dry faster on a warm, windy day than on a cold, still day. Why?
options: The clothes melt in the warmth
Warmth and wind both increase the rate of evaporation
Cold air makes water evaporate faster
Wind adds water to the clothes
questions.hint: Think about what speeds up evaporation.
questions.explanation: Higher temperature gives particles more energy, and wind carries water vapour away, so evaporation is faster.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: At what temperature does pure water boil at sea level?

mistakes.3: 212 is the boiling point in °F, not °C

questions.hint: It is a round number in °C.
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C at sea level.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Chocolate melts in your hand but not in the fridge. What does this tell you?
options: Its melting point is between fridge temperature and body temperature
questions.explanation: Your hand (about 37 °C) is above chocolate’s melting point; the fridge is below it.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which is a gas at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is a gas at room temperature.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does steam on a bathroom mirror turn into water droplets?
options: The steam cools on the mirror and condenses
questions.explanation: Water vapour cools on the cold mirror and condenses into liquid water.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why are winter coats often filled with feathers or fibres that trap air?
options: Air conducts heat into the body
Trapped air is a good thermal insulator, reducing heat loss
questions.explanation: Trapped air is a poor conductor of heat, so it slows heat loss from the body.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How would you separate sand from water?
questions.hint: Filter paper lets water through but not the sand grains.
questions.explanation: Filtering traps sand on the filter paper while water passes through.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is an irreversible change?

mistakes.3: Dissolving is reversible — evaporating the water gets the sugar back

questions.hint: Which one makes new materials that cannot be changed back?
questions.explanation: Burning makes new substances (ash, smoke, gases) and cannot be reversed.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: When salt dissolves in water, what has happened?
options: The salt has turned into water
The salt has broken into tiny particles mixed among the water particles

mistakes.3: Melting needs heat; dissolving is mixing into a liquid
mistakes.0: The salt is still there — the water tastes salty

questions.hint: Taste the water — is the salt still there?
questions.explanation: The salt is still present but spread out as tiny particles: a solution.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How could you get the salt back from salty water?

mistakes.1: Dissolved salt passes straight through filter paper

questions.explanation: Evaporating the water leaves the salt crystals behind.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How could you separate iron filings from sand?
questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic and sand is not.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which change will make sugar dissolve faster in water?
questions.hint: Think about temperature, stirring and particle size.
questions.explanation: Warm water and stirring both speed up dissolving (as do smaller grains).

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A student says “Cooking an egg is a reversible change because the egg is still an egg.” Is she right?
options: Yes — the egg can be cooled back to raw
No — cooking makes new substances; the egg cannot be made raw again
Yes — all changes involving heat are reversible
questions.explanation: Cooking permanently changes the egg — it is an irreversible change.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You have a mixture of rice, salt and water. Which order of steps separates all three?
options: Sieve out the rice, then evaporate the water to leave salt
Filter the salt, then sieve the water
questions.explanation: A sieve removes the rice; evaporating the salty water leaves the salt.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which word describes a solid that does NOT dissolve in water?
questions.explanation: An insoluble substance does not dissolve.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is a reversible change?
questions.explanation: Melted chocolate can be cooled to become solid again.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which equipment separates large stones from fine soil?
questions.explanation: A sieve lets the fine soil through and keeps the large stones.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does more sugar dissolve in hot tea than in cold tea?
options: Cold tea is already full of sugar
Particles move faster in hot liquids, so sugar dissolves faster and more of it can dissolve
questions.explanation: In hotter liquids particles move faster, so the solid dissolves faster and more can dissolve before the solution is saturated.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the unit used to measure force?
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N) using a forcemeter.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A ball rolling across the grass slows down and stops. Which force causes this?
questions.hint: This force acts between surfaces that rub.
questions.explanation: Friction between the ball and grass acts against the motion and slows the ball down.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the pull of gravity on it (N)
Weight is measured in kg and mass in newtons
Mass changes on the Moon but weight does not

mistakes.2: It is the other way round: weight changes, mass stays the same

questions.hint: One is measured in kg, the other in N.
questions.explanation: Mass (kg) stays the same everywhere; weight (N) depends on gravity.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: An astronaut goes to the Moon. What happens to her mass and weight?
options: Her mass is less; her weight stays the same
Her mass stays the same; her weight is less
questions.explanation: Mass does not change, but weaker gravity means her weight is less.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A boat floats on water. Which two forces are balanced?
questions.hint: One pulls down, one pushes up.
questions.explanation: The boat’s weight acts down and upthrust from the water acts up; they are balanced.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does a parachute slow a skydiver down?
options: Its large surface area increases air resistance
It increases upthrust from the ground
questions.hint: More surface pushing against the air…
questions.explanation: The large canopy pushes against lots of air, increasing air resistance.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Two people push a box from opposite sides. One pushes with 30 N, the other with 50 N. What happens?
options: The box moves towards the person pushing with 30 N
The box moves towards the person pushing with 50 N
The box stays still because both are pushing
questions.explanation: There is an unbalanced force of 20 N in the direction of the 50 N push — towards the person pushing with 30 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A car is moving at a steady speed on a straight road. What can you say about the forces on it?
options: The driving force and the resistive forces are balanced
The driving force is much bigger than friction

mistakes.2: Forces still act, but they are balanced

questions.hint: Steady speed means no change in motion.
questions.explanation: At a steady speed, forces are balanced: forward force = friction + air resistance.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which surface would give the most friction for a toy car?
questions.explanation: Carpet is the roughest surface, so it gives most friction.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which force pulls objects towards the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls objects towards the centre of the Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why are the soles of trainers made with a deep pattern?
options: To reduce friction so you run faster
To increase friction and stop slipping
questions.explanation: The pattern increases friction between the shoe and the ground.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A forcemeter shows that a rock weighs 12 N in air and 8 N when hanging in water. What is the size of the upthrust in newtons?
questions.explanation: 12 − 8 = 4 N of upthrust.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Look at the circuit. What would happen if one lamp was removed?
options: The other lamp stays the same
The other lamp goes out because the circuit is broken
questions.hint: In a series circuit there is only one path.
questions.explanation: In a series circuit the current has one path. Removing a lamp breaks the circuit, so the other lamp goes out.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which material is an electrical insulator?
questions.hint: Wires are covered in it for safety.
questions.explanation: Plastic does not let electricity flow through it easily.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What does a switch do in a circuit?
options: Opens or closes the circuit to stop or start the current
Changes the colour of the light
questions.hint: Think of turning a light on and off.
questions.explanation: A switch completes (closes) or breaks (opens) the circuit.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What happens to the brightness of lamps in a series circuit if you add another lamp?
options: Only the new lamp lights up
questions.hint: The same battery has to push current through more lamps.
questions.explanation: More lamps in series means more resistance and less current, so each lamp is dimmer.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What happens if you add a second battery (cell) in series to a circuit with one lamp?
questions.explanation: Two cells give a greater voltage, so more current flows and the lamp is brighter.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which pair of magnet poles will attract each other?
questions.explanation: Opposite poles attract; like poles repel.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which object would be attracted to a magnet?

mistakes.1: Aluminium is a metal but it is not magnetic

questions.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material. Aluminium and copper are metals but not magnetic.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A lamp in a circuit does not light. Which is the most sensible first check?
options: Check that all the connections are complete and the switch is closed
questions.hint: A circuit must be a complete loop.
questions.explanation: A gap in the circuit (loose wire or open switch) is the most common reason a lamp does not light.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How could you test whether a pencil “lead” (graphite) conducts electricity?
options: Put it in a gap in a working circuit with a lamp and see if the lamp lights
questions.hint: Use a circuit as a tester.
questions.explanation: If the lamp lights when the material completes the circuit, it is a conductor. (Graphite does conduct.)

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is a good electrical conductor?
questions.explanation: Copper is a metal and a good conductor.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Two lamps are connected in series with one cell. One lamp’s filament breaks. What happens?
options: Only the broken lamp goes out
questions.hint: Is there still a complete loop?
questions.explanation: The circuit is broken, so no current flows and both lamps go out.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why do magnets push apart when two north poles face each other?
questions.explanation: Like poles (N–N or S–S) repel.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How do we see an object such as a book?
options: Light from a source reflects off the book into our eyes
We see it because of sound waves
Light travels from our eyes to the book
The book gives out its own light

mistakes.2: Eyes receive light; they do not send it out

questions.hint: Most objects are not light sources.
questions.explanation: Light from a source (like the Sun or a lamp) reflects off the book and enters our eyes.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does a shadow form behind an object?
options: Shadows are made of dark light
The object blocks light, which travels in straight lines
The object reflects all the light backwards
questions.hint: Light cannot go through an opaque object.
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines; an opaque object blocks it, leaving a dark area behind.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which of these is a light source?

mistakes.1: The Moon reflects light from the Sun

questions.explanation: A candle flame produces its own light; the Moon and mirrors only reflect light.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How are sounds made?
questions.explanation: All sounds are made by vibrations.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A guitar string is tightened. What happens to the sound?
questions.explanation: A tighter string vibrates faster, giving a higher pitch.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A torch is moved closer to an object. What happens to the shadow on the screen behind?
questions.hint: The object blocks more of the light spreading from the torch.
questions.explanation: Closer to the light source, the object blocks a wider cone of light, so the shadow is bigger.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why can sound not travel through space?
options: Sound needs particles (a medium) to travel through, and space is a vacuum
questions.hint: Sound is passed on by vibrating particles.
questions.explanation: Sound travels as vibrations passed between particles. Space has almost no particles.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A pencil in a glass of water looks bent at the surface. Why?
options: Light changes direction (refracts) as it passes from water to air
questions.hint: Light travels at different speeds in different materials.
questions.explanation: Light refracts (bends) as it passes between water and air, so the pencil appears bent.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which material would be best for soundproofing a music room?
questions.explanation: Soft, thick materials absorb sound vibrations instead of reflecting them.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What happens to light when it hits a mirror?
questions.explanation: Mirrors reflect light.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Hitting a drum harder makes the sound…
options: louder, because the vibrations are bigger
questions.explanation: Hitting harder makes bigger vibrations, so the sound is louder.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: You see lightning before you hear the thunder. What does this tell you?
options: Thunder happens after the lightning has finished
Light travels much faster than sound
Your eyes work faster than your ears
questions.hint: They happen at the same time.
questions.explanation: Both are made at the same moment, but light reaches you almost instantly; sound is much slower.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What causes day and night on Earth?
options: The Earth spinning on its axis
The Sun moving around the Earth

mistakes.1: Orbiting the Sun takes a year and causes the year, not day and night
mistakes.3: The Sun appears to move because the Earth spins

questions.explanation: The Earth rotates once every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day; the side facing away has night.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which type of rock forms when lava or magma cools?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten rock cools and solidifies.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How long does it take the Earth to orbit the Sun?

mistakes.3: That is roughly the Moon’s cycle

questions.explanation: One orbit takes about 365¼ days — one year.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.hint: It is the smallest planet too.
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does the Moon appear to change shape during a month?
options: The Earth’s shadow covers parts of it each night
We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits the Earth

mistakes.1: That only happens in a lunar eclipse

questions.hint: Half the Moon is always lit by the Sun.
questions.explanation: As the Moon orbits, we see different parts of its sunlit side — the phases.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which type of rock often contains fossils?
questions.hint: It forms from layers of sediment.
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rock forms in layers that can trap the remains of living things.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the Earth’s outermost solid layer called?
questions.explanation: The crust is the thin rocky outer layer.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why are there seasons on Earth?
options: The Earth’s axis is tilted, so each hemisphere gets more direct sunlight at different times of the year
The Earth is much closer to the Sun in summer
The Sun gets hotter in summer
The Moon blocks sunlight in winter

mistakes.1: A common misconception — the tilt matters, not the distance

questions.hint: Think about the tilt of the axis.
questions.explanation: Because of the tilt, a hemisphere tilted towards the Sun gets longer days and more direct light — summer.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why do earthquakes and volcanoes often happen in the same places?
options: They are caused by the Moon
They happen near the sea only
They happen where the plates of the Earth’s crust meet and move
They happen where it is hottest on the surface
questions.hint: The crust is broken into pieces.
questions.explanation: Most occur at plate boundaries, where pieces of the crust move against, apart from, or under each other.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is the Sun?
questions.hint: It gives out its own light.
questions.explanation: The Sun is a star.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why does the Sun appear to move across the sky during the day?
options: Because the Sun orbits the Earth daily
questions.explanation: The Earth’s rotation makes the Sun appear to rise in the east and set in the west.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Soil A drains water quickly; soil B holds water for a long time. Soil A is most likely…
questions.explanation: Sandy soil has large particles with big gaps, so water drains through quickly.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Ravi tests whether the height a ball is dropped from affects how high it bounces. Which variable should he change?

mistakes.0: That is what he measures (dependent variable)

questions.hint: The variable you change is the one you are testing.
questions.explanation: The independent variable — the one he changes — is the drop height.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why should Ravi use the same ball and the same floor each time?
options: To make it a fair test, so only drop height affects the result
Because balls only bounce on floors
questions.explanation: Keeping other variables the same (control variables) means any change is caused only by the drop height.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In an investigation, what is the dependent variable?
options: The variables you keep the same
questions.hint: It depends on what you change.
questions.explanation: The dependent variable is what you measure or observe.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Mia investigates how the temperature of water affects how quickly sugar dissolves. What should she measure?
options: The time for the sugar to dissolve
questions.hint: How will she know how quickly it dissolves?
questions.explanation: She measures the time taken — the dependent variable.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: In Mia’s investigation, which should be a control variable?
questions.explanation: The volume of water should stay the same so the test is fair.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which is the best prediction for an investigation into ramp height and toy car distance?
options: The higher the ramp, the further the car will travel, because it will be going faster at the bottom
questions.hint: A good prediction says what will happen and why.
questions.explanation: A scientific prediction links the variables and gives a reason.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Why is it a good idea to repeat measurements in an investigation?
options: Because the first result is always wrong
To make the investigation take longer
To check results and reduce the effect of errors, so the results are more reliable
To get different answers each time
questions.hint: What if one result is unusual?
questions.explanation: Repeating lets you spot anomalous results and calculate an average, making results more reliable.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which equipment is best for measuring 50 ml of water accurately?
questions.explanation: A measuring cylinder measures volume accurately.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Leo tests which paper towel absorbs most water. He uses a different volume of water for each towel. What is wrong?
options: It is not a fair test because the volume of water should be the same
questions.hint: What should be kept the same?
questions.explanation: Changing the volume of water as well as the towel means he cannot tell which caused the difference.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: What is a safety risk when heating water in a beaker, and how can it be reduced?
options: Burns or scalds — wear goggles, let it cool and use heat-proof gloves or tongs
questions.explanation: Hot water can cause scalds. Using tongs, eye protection and care reduces the risk.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: An investigation tests whether the number of turns on a spinner’s wings affects how long it takes to fall. What is the independent variable?
options: The height it is dropped from
The number of turns (the change made to the wings)
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor that is changed on purpose.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A student wants to find which plant food helps plants grow tallest. Which plan is fairest?
options: Use identical plants, the same amount of water and light, and change only the plant food
Put some plants inside and some outside
Give each plant a different amount of water and food
Use different plants for each food
questions.explanation: Only the plant food should change; everything else stays the same.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Predict how the length of a pendulum string affects the time for one swing.
options: A longer string will swing faster
A longer string will take longer to swing, because the bob travels a longer path
String length makes no difference to anything
questions.hint: Think of a playground swing with long chains.
questions.explanation: A longer pendulum takes more time for each swing.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Look at the table. What pattern does it show?
options: As water temperature increases, the time to dissolve decreases
As water temperature increases, the time to dissolve increases
questions.explanation: Higher temperature → shorter time. Sugar dissolves faster in hotter water.

stimulus.caption: Time for one spoon of sugar to dissolve

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Using the table, estimate the time for sugar to dissolve at 50 °C.
questions.explanation: Between 75 s (40 °C) and 42 s (60 °C) — about halfway, so roughly 55–60 s. Answers from 46 to 70 s are accepted.

stimulus.caption: Time for one spoon of sugar to dissolve

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which result in the table is most likely to be anomalous?
questions.hint: Look for a value that does not fit the pattern.
questions.explanation: Plant B grows 2, 3, 4, then 12, then 6 — the 12 cm reading does not fit the steady pattern.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How much did Plant A grow between week 1 and week 5?

mistakes.12: Gave the final height, not the growth

questions.hint: Subtract the week 1 height from the week 5 height.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Which type of graph is best for showing how a plant’s height changes over several weeks?
questions.hint: The data changes continuously over time.
questions.explanation: Line graphs show how a measurement changes over time.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Three repeat measurements of a ball’s bounce were 42 cm, 46 cm and 44 cm. What is the mean?

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Describe what the graph shows.
options: The water cools at a steady rate
The water cools quickly at first, then more slowly
questions.hint: Compare the drop in the first 5 minutes with the last 5.
questions.explanation: It drops 18 °C in the first 5 minutes but only 5 °C in the last 5 — cooling slows down.

stimulus.caption: Temperature of a cup of water as it cools

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Use the graph to predict the temperature of the water after 25 minutes.
questions.hint: The drop is getting smaller each time.
questions.explanation: Drops are 18, 12, 8, 5 … the next drop will be about 3, so about 33–35 °C. Answers from 31 to 37 are accepted.

stimulus.caption: Temperature of a cup of water as it cools

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A student concludes: “Plants grow best in red light.” She tested one plant in red light and one in blue light. Why is her conclusion weak?
options: She tested only one plant in each colour, so the result could be due to chance
She should have used no light
questions.hint: How much evidence did she collect?
questions.explanation: With only one plant per condition, differences could be due to that individual plant. More plants and repeats are needed.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: How could the student improve the investigation into light colour?
options: Use several plants for each colour and repeat the measurements
Change the amount of water as well
Use one plant for both colours at the same time
questions.explanation: More plants and repeats give more reliable results.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: The bar chart shows how far paper planes flew. Which design flew furthest?
questions.explanation: The glider flew 8.2 m — the furthest.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Using the same bar chart, how much further did the Glider fly than the Stunt plane?

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: A table shows that the more a spring is stretched by masses, the longer it gets. Which conclusion is best?
options: The spring will always be 11 cm
The spring gets shorter with more mass
The length increases by 2 cm for every 100 g added
questions.hint: Look at how much it increases each time.
questions.explanation: Each extra 100 g adds 2 cm — a steady pattern.

questions.subject: science
questions.prompt: Using the spring table, predict the length of the spring with 400 g.
